title: Prefix each WMBT sequence with one of the nine step codes

facts.note: Planner writes, edits, renames or reviews a WMBT artifact or its sequence prefix.
WMBT files/URNs identifiable by path and filename pattern.
Task text mentions WMBTs or their step codes.
Letter-set membership is mechanically checkable on filename/URN; whether the letter matches the step's intent (including after a body edit changes that intent) is llm_judged.

fires: Planner authors a new WMBT and must pick its step-code prefix for the URN/filename.
Planner renames or re-sequences an existing WMBT.
Planner edits a WMBT's body so that the step's intent changes, making the existing prefix potentially wrong.
Planner or reviewer evaluates an existing WMBT whose prefix is a valid letter but does not match the step's intent.
A WMBT URN or filename uses a prefix letter outside D L P C E M Y R K.
doesNotFire: Editing WMBT body text (wording, examples) without changing the step's intent and without touching its URN, filename or step code.
Authoring wagons, acceptances or docs that neither name nor imply a WMBT sequence prefix.
Coder or tester work on implementation files that do not name WMBTs.

given: A WMBT sequence prefix (in its URN and filename) is being selected, changed, or evaluated.
when: The planner chooses or checks the single-letter step code that prefixes the WMBT sequence.
then: Use exactly one code from D L P C E M Y R K, the one whose step intent matches the WMBT: D define (requirements, criteria, constraints), L locate (discover/find resources), P prepare (setup/configure prerequisites), C confirm (verify/validate conditions), E execute (perform/run the main action), M monitor (observe/track progress), Y modify (update/adjust state), R resolve (fix/handle issues), K conclude (complete/finalize).
prefer: Pick the letter by the step's intent from the code table, not by the first letter of the verb (modify is Y, conclude is K).
Use the same code consistently in the WMBT URN and its filename.
avoid: Inventing letters or multi-letter codes outside the nine-code vocabulary.
Choosing a code by spelling (e.g. M for modify, C for conclude) instead of by the defined mapping.
Defaulting every WMBT to E to avoid deciding the step's intent.
why: WMBT URNs and filenames embed the step code, so a closed, shared letter→intent vocabulary keeps WMBT identifiers parseable and the step's purpose readable from its id.
evidence: Every WMBT URN/filename step-code prefix is a member of {D, L, P, C, E, M, Y, R, K}.
Reviewer confirms the chosen letter's intent (per the code table) matches what the WMBT step does, including for existing WMBTs whose body was edited.
verifier_detail: Closed vocabulary (term_id step_code, label 'Step codes', 'letter -> step name + intent.'): D=define, L=locate, P=prepare, C=confirm, E=execute, M=monitor, Y=modify, R=resolve, K=conclude. Single uppercase letter; anything else is a finding.

Intent glosses: D Define requirements, criteria, or constraints; L Locate, discover, or find resources; P Prepare, setup, or configure prerequisites; C Confirm, verify, or validate conditions; E Execute, perform, or run the main action; M Monitor, observe, or track progress; Y Modify, update, or adjust state; R Resolve, fix, or handle issues; K Conclude, complete, or finalize.
